claim.why_it_matters: This page otherwise preserves indentation with '    ', but the four sub-entries that open the second print column lose it, so READ/RETURN/STRING/UNSTRING read as top-level entries instead of continuing the 'INTO phrase' list broken by the column break.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by direct pixel measurement of the 300dpi render, not by eyeballing. The index on p1247 prints exactly two indent levels per column, separated by a constant 72px at 300dpi (~0.24in, the four-space sub-entry indent). Left column tail: 'INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING clause 278', 'Internal items 168', 'International date and time 1166' and 'INTO phrase' all start at x=337 (level 0), while 'DIVIDE statement 614' starts at x=409 (level 1). Right column: its level-0 origin is x=1342 ('Intrinsic function summary 806', 'Intrinsic functions 796', 'INVALID clause 413', ...) and its level-1 origin is x=1414. The first four lines of the right column -- READ statement 692 (y=388), RETURN statement 708 (y=433), STRING statement 759 (y=477), UNSTRING statement 769 (y=522) -- all measure xstart=1413/1414, i.e. level 1. The very next line, 'Intrinsic function summary 806' (y=566), measures xstart=1342, i.e. level 0. So the PDF unambiguously prints those four as sub-entries continuing the 'INTO phrase' list across the column break, and the printed glyph positions rule out any reading in which they are top-level entries. Both quotations in the claim are accurate: markdown line 63 carries the ' 'x4 prefix on 'DIVIDE statement [614]', and markdown lines 65-68 (file lines 51653-51656 of specs/ISO_COBOL.md) carry no prefix at all, making them textually indistinguishable from line 69 'Intrinsic function summary [806]', which is a genuine level-0 entry. This is not page-break furniture, wrapping, or hyphenation: in an index, indentation IS the content -- it encodes the parent/child relation -- and this same transcription preserves it correctly on 58 other lines of this very page, including the immediately preceding line. The flattening changes meaning: it orphans four sub-entries from their 'INTO phrase' parent and asserts four spurious top-level index entries. I considered and rejected 'formatting only' on that basis. Note the blank markdown line 64 is by itself legitimate column-break furniture and is not the defect; the defect is solely the four missing indent prefixes.
verdict.corrected_description: Claim is accurate as filed; only sharpening the evidence and scope. On markdown lines 65-68 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 51653-51656) the four index sub-entries READ statement 692, RETURN statement 708, STRING statement 759 and UNSTRING statement 769 lose their ' 'x4 sub-entry prefix. The PDF prints all four at the level-1 indent (measured xstart=1413/1414 vs the right column's level-0 origin x=1342, a constant 72px/0.24in delta matching the left column's 337 -> 409), continuing the 'INTO phrase' list that the print column break splits after 'DIVIDE statement 614'. Without the prefix they are typeset identically to the genuine level-0 entry 'Intrinsic function summary [806]' on the next line, so the transcription flattens four children of 'INTO phrase' into four false top-level entries. Fix: prepend '    ' to those four lines. The intervening blank line (md line 64) is correct column-break furniture and should be left alone. Severity 'cosmetic' is right -- this is index navigation only and touches no normative text. Sibling lead, unverified and out of scope for this page: several other flush-left 'READ statement [692]' index lines earlier in the file (e.g. lines 50056, 50058, 50231, sitting under 'ADVANCING ON LOCK phrase', 'ADVANCING phrase' and 'AT END phrase') look like the same indent loss on other index pages and may warrant a sweep against their own PDF renders.
